requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted (LUKS) volume on node1
requirements.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat --type luks2 succeeded on a file-backed image, followed by a successful luksOpen creating /dev/mapper/secure_srv.
ext4 filesystem created on the mapper device and mounted at /srv/secure; a test file was written and read back, and post-reboot df/lsblk confirm the mount from /dev/mapper/secure_srv.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot with no manual intervention
requirements.summary: crypttab/fstab entries were added, systemd generated systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount pulled into local-fs.target. A genuine node reboot was triggered (systemctl reboot), boot_id changed from f9bf293d... to e7733aa3..., and post-restart evidence shows systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service succeeded automatically, srv-secure.mount is active, and the pre-existing test file content ('hello') was intact — demonstrating the full boot-time unlock/mount transition without manual action.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes are fully satisfied: a LUKS2-encrypted volume was created, mounted at /srv/secure, configured via crypttab/fstab for automatic unlock and mount, and this was directly verified by a genuine full-node reboot (confirmed via changed boot_id) followed by evidence that the volume auto-unlocked, auto-mounted, and preserved data with no manual intervention. Operational hygiene is clean with no unnecessary or unreverted mutations.
limitations: The keyfile enabling automatic unlock is stored unencrypted on the root filesystem (root-only permissions); this is an inherent trade-off for boot-time auto-unlock without a TPM/network-bound mechanism and was not flagged as an issue by the task, but represents a lower security bar than passphrase-only LUKS.
Evidence for the reboot is a single successful cycle; no additional failure-mode testing (e.g., missing keyfile, corrupted image) was performed, though none was required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: keyfile creation, image creation, LUKS format/open, filesystem creation and mount, crypttab/fstab edits, and the umount+luksClose/systemctl start cycle used only to verify the generator-created units work before trusting a real reboot. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; failed-services lists are empty both before and after, and listening-socket/temp-file diffs are attributable solely to the reboot itself (new ephemeral PIDs/private-tmp dirs), not to executor actions. The keyfile is root-only (chmod 600) and crypttab/fstab entries use nofail, avoiding boot risk.
